chunks.title: RKA-Lab
chunks.text: Evaluation library for tracing remembered evidence from recognition through recall, source recollection, and action. RKA-Lab evaluates four matched rungs against the same evidence and compares them with irrelevant-memory and gold-memory masks, separating fluent answers from evidence-linked memory that changes behavior.

chunks.title: RKA-Lab — limitation
chunks.text: The included 10-item snapshot verifies the software path; it is not the planned full benchmark or a publication result.

chunks.title: TxnMem
chunks.text: Transactional shared memory with explicit update semantics and replayable histories for concurrent agent teams. TxnMem models facts, constraints, resources, commitments, evidence, and commutative values as typed operations, then checks accepted histories against a deterministic serial interpreter.

chunks.title: TxnMem — limitation
chunks.text: The repository identifies itself as a research prototype and does not claim production readiness.

chunks.title: ChronicleGuard
chunks.text: Source-aware multimodal recall evaluation that keeps episodic evidence separate from mutable beliefs.

chunks.title: ChronicleGuard — limitation
chunks.text: The default evaluation uses original synthetic scenes; external vision-language models are optional.

chunks.title: IntentLedger
chunks.text: Cancellation-safe prospective memory built on an append-only lifecycle ledger.

chunks.title: IntentLedger — limitation
chunks.text: The included lifecycle benchmark is synthetic and does not validate deployment in an autonomous production agent.

chunks.title: FreshIndex
chunks.text: Capacity-aware scheduling for proactive verification of mutable agent memories. FreshIndex assigns each memory an age-aware audit priority, explains that score, dispatches only approved verifiers, and records decisions in a tamper-evident event log.

chunks.title: FreshIndex — limitation
chunks.text: Included simulations support engineering checks; policy effectiveness on live memory streams remains an open evaluation question.

chunks.title: RecallResolve
chunks.text: Evidence-first resolution of exact consumer-product recall variants with active multimodal evidence acquisition.

chunks.title: RecallResolve — limitation
chunks.text: The local source is an implementation brief; implementation and evaluation details are not asserted in this catalog.

chunks.title: HippoGate
chunks.text: Belief-state control for deciding whether to forget, probe, retain, or consolidate a candidate memory. HippoGate treats cross-context applicability as a hidden state and makes each consolidation decision traceable to its posterior, cost model, recurrence estimate, horizon, and probe likelihoods.

chunks.title: HippoGate — limitation
chunks.text: The decision model depends on configured costs and likelihoods and is not a general safety guarantee.

chunks.title: HypothesisOps
chunks.text: Safe sequential search over competing causal explanations for simulated cloud incidents.

chunks.title: HypothesisOps — limitation
chunks.text: The system operates in a deterministic simulator and does not connect to production services.

chunks.title: MethodChain
chunks.text: Evidence-governed reconstruction of experimental procedures spread across citations and supporting files.

chunks.title: MethodChain — limitation
chunks.text: The output is not validated for laboratory execution and does not provide safety approval.

chunks.title: ChangePilot
chunks.text: Version-aware Python API migration analysis with conservative edits and closed-world verification.

chunks.title: ChangePilot — limitation
chunks.text: The prototype is not a replacement for a project test suite or a general-purpose refactoring platform.

chunks.title: MemEquiv
chunks.text: Executable metamorphic contracts for persistent agent memory. MemEquiv checks whether histories related by a declared transformation preserve the right facts, uncertainty, scope, provenance, and future behavior across memory adapters.

chunks.title: MemEquiv — limitation
chunks.text: Passing the included contracts is evidence about tested relations, not proof of safety or correctness in every deployment.

chunks.title: CurriGraph
chunks.text: Directed transfer graphs for online curriculum selection in tool agents.

chunks.title: CurriGraph — limitation
chunks.text: Synthetic diagnostics do not establish general performance on real agents.

chunks.title: Communicate to Remember
chunks.text: Contextual-bandit routing that jointly chooses communication and memory actions for multi-agent systems.

chunks.title: Communicate to Remember — limitation
chunks.text: The included evaluation is a controlled simulation and does not establish effectiveness in deployed agent teams.

chunks.title: ScopeGuard
chunks.text: Argument-level memory non-interference checks for tool-using agents.

chunks.title: ScopeGuard — limitation
chunks.text: Authorization depends on explicit scope, source, authority, purpose, and evidence declarations.

chunks.title: WorldModel-L*
chunks.text: Active symbolic world-model induction for learning hidden tool behavior before committing to a plan.

chunks.title: WorldModel-L* — limitation
chunks.text: The bounded version space represents configured hypotheses, not every possible hidden tool behavior.

chunks.title: LineageRAG
chunks.text: Copy-aware evidence corroboration that groups dependent documents before verification. LineageRAG infers likely document derivation links, collapses dependent documents into origin families, and combines evidence at the family level instead of counting copied URLs as independent support.

chunks.title: LineageRAG — limitation
chunks.text: Copy-family inference is probabilistic; corroboration quality depends on lineage and stance estimates.

chunks.title: RobustAsk
chunks.text: Reliability-aware clarification when user answers may be noisy, changing, or systematically confused.

chunks.title: RobustAsk — limitation
chunks.text: Smoke-scale and synthetic results do not establish general performance with real users.

chunks.title: FALSIFY
chunks.text: Active minimal-counterexample discovery for selective procedural memory.

chunks.title: FALSIFY — limitation
chunks.text: The repository does not claim that active search beats a strong judge on unseen operator families.

chunks.title: RegimeBank
chunks.text: Separate memory banks for recurring operating regimes in non-stationary environments.

chunks.title: RegimeBank — limitation
chunks.text: The included benchmark is controlled and does not cover every form of non-stationarity.

chunks.title: MemIntervene
chunks.text: Replay-defined causal evaluation of how stored memories change later agent actions.

chunks.title: MemIntervene — limitation
chunks.text: Current results are smoke-scale engineering results, not evidence for broad causal claims.

chunks.title: CertiCompress
chunks.text: Proof-carrying consolidation for action-coupled agent memory.

chunks.title: CertiCompress — limitation
chunks.text: Certificates cover configured semantic checks and replay probes rather than every downstream behavior.

chunks.title: TEMPO-Trust
chunks.text: Claim-conditioned online source reliability under drift, copying, and delayed feedback.

chunks.title: TEMPO-Trust — limitation
chunks.text: Trust estimates remain conditional on available audits, copy detection, and configured regimes.

chunks.title: TempoRAGS
chunks.text: Reader-aware parallel anytime reranker-guided graph search under latency budgets. TempoRAGS studies how several complementary document-graph frontier regions can be reranked in parallel while an anytime controller returns the best valid ranking before a deadline.

chunks.title: TempoRAGS — limitation
chunks.text: Included measurements are engineering smoke results, not public-benchmark or publication results.

chunks.title: ParamLedger
chunks.text: Evidence-governed promotion and rollback for parametric memory updates.

chunks.title: ParamLedger — limitation
chunks.text: The deterministic reference path does not establish safe promotion for arbitrary model updates.

chunks.title: VerifySplit
chunks.text: Independent-evidence controls for shared failure in generator-verifier systems. VerifySplit studies failures where a generator and verifier agree because they inherit the same model, trajectory, or evidence error, using explicit provenance and independent evidence paths.

chunks.title: VerifySplit — limitation
chunks.text: The included smoke results verify the artifact path and do not establish the full research thesis.

chunks.title: EvidRoute
chunks.text: Risk-constrained sequential routing across heterogeneous evidence sources.

chunks.title: EvidRoute — limitation
chunks.text: Risk and stopping behavior are evaluated within configured source and shift models.

chunks.title: TraceMem
chunks.text: Causal reliability maps for persistent agents using fault injection, counterfactual replay, and pre-commit verification.

chunks.title: TraceMem — limitation
chunks.text: Only repository-level public metadata is represented; detailed implementation and evaluation claims are intentionally omitted.

chunks.title: BarrierNow
chunks.text: Fresh-evidence route previews under temporary, uncertain, and time-sensitive mobility barriers.

chunks.title: BarrierNow — limitation
chunks.text: BarrierNow is not safety certification or emergency navigation and does not establish that a route is safe for a person.

chunks.title: WhoFixesThis
chunks.text: Temporal responsibility search for evidence-based civic service routing.

chunks.title: WhoFixesThis — limitation
chunks.text: The demo is not government guidance and never submits a report.

chunks.title: Profile — Identity
chunks.text: Pankit Brahmkhatri is a Master's CS student at TU Dresden.

chunks.title: Profile — Research focus
chunks.text: His research focuses on agent memory, information retrieval, test-time learning, search-guided reasoning, and reliable tool agents. He builds research prototypes and evaluation systems, and presents their evidence, assumptions, and limitations explicitly.

chunks.title: Research overview — Central research question
chunks.text: How can an agent turn remembered or retrieved evidence into a reliable action when sources can be incomplete, stale, conflicting, or wrong? The portfolio approaches this as an end-to-end systems question spanning memory, retrieval, adaptation, reasoning, tools, and evaluation.

chunks.title: Research overview — Research method
chunks.text: The projects make evidence boundaries visible, record provenance and time, test interventions or counterfactuals where possible, and distinguish deterministic software checks from broader research claims. They favor calibrated clarification or abstention when the indexed evidence is insufficient.

chunks.title: Research overview — Shared system view
chunks.text: The shared framing is memory as a decision system. Across the portfolio, reliable behavior depends on more than storing facts: an agent must recognize relevant evidence, recall it at the right moment, identify its source, decide whether it is still valid, and use it to choose an appropriate action.

chunks.title: Research themes — Agent memory and adaptation
chunks.text: This theme studies what an agent should retain, consolidate, correct, or forget. It treats memory as a controlled state that must remain useful across changing contexts rather than as an unbounded transcript.

chunks.title: Research themes — Information retrieval and evidence
chunks.text: This theme studies recall, source recollection, provenance, temporal validity, and selective evidence acquisition. The goal is to retrieve evidence that is not merely similar to a query, but relevant, attributable, and timely enough to support a decision.

chunks.title: Research themes — Test-time learning
chunks.text: This theme studies safe adaptation during use, including when repeated observations justify parameter promotion and when uncertain evidence should stay outside persistent model state. Adaptation is evaluated as a governed process rather than an automatic update.

chunks.title: Research themes — Search-guided reasoning
chunks.text: This theme treats reasoning as a search over hypotheses, evidence requests, and possible actions. Search should expose uncertainty, respect constraints, and stop with clarification or abstention when the available evidence cannot support a reliable choice.

chunks.title: Research themes — Reliable tool agents
chunks.text: This theme studies agents that act through tools under concurrency, scope, and failure. Reliability depends on typed state changes, causal influence tests, pre-action verification, and traceable boundaries between observation, decision, and effect.

chunks.title: Research connection map — Indexed catalog
chunks.text: The catalog count is generated from the authoritative project records, keeping verified public projects separate from pending title-only entries. The portfolio has 34 indexed project records: 29 verified public projects and 5 pending title-only records.

chunks.title: Research connection map — Recognition, recall, source, and action
chunks.text: RKA-Lab connects four evaluation rungs: recognizing remembered evidence, recalling it, identifying its source, and using it to choose an action. The distinction separates fluent answers from memory that causally changes behavior.

chunks.title: Research connection map — Concurrency and temporal validity
chunks.text: TxnMem studies concurrent updates to shared agent memory. FreshIndex schedules checks when mutable memories may be stale, while RegimeBank tracks whether experience remains valid after a regime change. Together they connect concurrency control with temporal validity.

chunks.title: Research connection map — Consolidation, correction, and forgetting
chunks.text: HippoGate decides whether to retain, probe, consolidate, or forget a candidate memory. MemEquiv tests whether a correction really changes behavior, and CertiCompress asks whether consolidation preserves the constraints that matter.

chunks.title: Research connection map — Causal influence, scope, and provenance
chunks.text: MemIntervene measures causal influence by intervening on memory. ScopeGuard limits where learned instructions apply, and CertiCompress preserves provenance through compression. Trace-Mem is connected only at the verified public metadata level; detailed implementation and evaluation claims are intentionally not inferred.

chunks.title: Research connection map — Parameter promotion
chunks.text: ParamLedger studies parameter promotion: moving repeated, supported observations into a more persistent state while keeping evidence, timing, and rollback information available for review.

chunks.title: Site scope and navigation — Indexed source boundary

chunks.text: Answers should identify the source that supports a claim, preserve project caveats, and distinguish verified repository evidence from title-only pending records. When the indexed sources do not support an answer, the assistant should say so plainly.
